summary: PASS: the OMN-17942 ticket-creation admission gate now bounds VOLUME as well as SHAPE. Rules 1-7 answer 'is this ticket bound to a commitment?' from the payload alone, which lets a parent accumulate an unbounded queue of correctly-bound tickets nobody will ever start -- every one of them admitted. The friction trend report of 2026-09-13 measured tickets created against tickets Done at 3.1 : 1 over fifteen days, a net +815, with 31 of 58 new friction tickets never started, across a window lying entirely AFTER that gate shipped on 2026-09-05. Rule 8 refuses a create whose named parent already carries more than unstarted_children_cap children in an unstarted state. The cap is one declared constant in plugins/onex/hooks/config/ticket_creation_policy.json with its rationale beside it; the checker reads it from there, proven by a test that lowers the configured cap and asserts the same census then refuses. The refusal names the parent, the count, the cap and the oldest unstarted child with its filing date, and names three routes out: start a child, cancel a child, or record an operator RULING row in the rolling work ledger and cite it on the create. That citation is resolved the way OMN-17957's credential guard resolves a rotation consent -- canonical ledger path, the cited line exists, the row's second field is exactly RULING, and the row names this parent -- and a citation that fails any of those is refused with that reason named rather than silently ignored. There is no environment variable and no policy flag: a test asserts the module reads no environment beyond locating its read credential and the ledger root. Rule 8 is the one rule here that reads state outside the payload, through an injected lookup seam so the decision core stays a pure function of its arguments; its fail direction is stated in the module docstring and pinned by tests -- a lookup failure or a truncated census refuses, and an absent read credential is the one bounded fail-open, because refusing every create on a machine with no key would make rules 1-7 collateral damage of a missing key and get the whole guard disabled rather than repaired. No new hook, no new mask bit, no new registration: the rule runs through the existing PreToolUse decision-core invocation. Measured live and read-only on 2026-09-13T18:13:15Z, 59 parents across the workspace carry more than ten unstarted children; the deepest carries 62 and 28 of the 59 have an oldest unstarted child filed before 2026-06-01. That list is in the pull request body for the operator to decide whether ten is the right number.
